tiers.rule: a repository file outside registry/tests/assurance_lab/ is BEHAVIOURAL when lab code imports it, executes it, parses it as data or derives an expectation from any of its content other than an exactly-once anchor text; it is NON-BEHAVIOURAL when lab code reads it only through exactly-once anchor checks, its LF-normalised sha256 digest or an existence check. The catalogue pins every behavioural file and every anchor-read non-behavioural file (baseline.sources); an existence-only citation is listed unpinned
tiers.lab: every file under registry/tests/assurance_lab/ (the suites, test_lab_replay_corpus.py itself included, the helpers, the runner, the generator, the re-record and trace tools and the corpus documents) is a lab file and is pinned exactly: a changed or unpinned lab file is a FAIL until the catalogue is regenerated. The one exemption is SCENARIO_CATALOGUE.json, which cannot record its own digest: test_lab_replay_corpus checks it against the tree ([0], [3]) and against a fresh static build ([5]), and gen_catalogue.py --check against a fresh full build. The replay suite is pinned like every other lab file (it embeds nothing derived from its own digest, so there is no circularity), so an edit to that gate is a catalogue change too
tiers.drift: a changed lab file is a FAIL ('re-generate the catalogue'); a changed behavioural file is one named FAIL per file that lists the corpus documents replaying it and the re-record procedure; a changed pinned file in neither tier is a FAIL judged as behavioural until it is classified; a changed non-behavioural file prints 'SOURCE DRIFT (non-behavioural): <path>' and is not a failure, while every anchor in it is still checked exactly once; a pinned file that is missing FAILS in every tier (a non-behavioural one as 'pinned source missing: <path>', the others under their tier's failure, 'sha256 missing'); ECCO_LAB_STRICT_BASELINE=1 (the environment value '1' exactly) keeps the whole-baseline rule (any pinned difference FAILS, under the check-name prefix 'gen_catalogue drift rule (STRICT)'). Every corpus document is judged against its own source_digests plus its tier's TIER_SOURCES (the tier pins, recorded in baseline.sources)
tiers.method: derived from an audit-hook trace, not by hand, and repeatable with registry/tests/assurance_lab/trace_inputs.py (a command-line tool, standard library only, not a suite; it exits 1 on any difference from this table): a sitecustomize module on PYTHONPATH (inherited by the suites' own child processes) installs sys.addaudithook and logs every 'open' of a repository file with the in-repository caller frames (innermost first) and whether the import machinery is on the stack; every lab suite runs from the repository root as 'python -B <file>' with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 (the CI command line 'python <file>' plus the two switches that keep the trace from writing bytecode; CI adds neither) in quick mode and in extended mode (ECCO_LAB_EXTENDED=1), and every corpus document is replayed alone in its own process with only its tier module imported (the per-tier sets). Logged paths are case-folded on Windows and mapped back to the repository's own spelling. A read by the import machinery, or one whose innermost in-repository frames are not an anchor, digest, overlay or existence helper, is behavioural; reads only through _lab_trace.anchor_count (every call site checks exactly once or prints the line as information), _lab_trace.source_digest, a TreeReader digest, gen_catalogue's anchor count (anchor_str), run_lab.lf_digest, test_lab_replay_corpus's anchor helpers (anchor_hits, anchors_not_once), its existence helper (cited) or its drift-control overlay copy (comment_overlay: hashed and anchor-counted only) are non-behavioural, and a file read only by the existence helper is listed unpinned. Quick and extended runs read the same 75 non-lab files; the replays of the documents of one tier execute the same set. Between traces the run-time import guard catches a new import: _lab_trace.finish() checks sys.modules at the end of every suite and FAILS naming every repository module outside the lab that BEHAVIOURAL does not list, whether a suite, a lab helper, a shared simulator or the generator imported it, at module level or lazily (test_lab_replay_corpus [2] and test_lab_selftest_core also check it mid-run). The guard does not see a data read (an open of a file the lab does not import) or an import made only by a command-line tool outside the suites (run_lab.py, gen_catalogue.py, rerecord_corpus.py); those are found by re-running trace_inputs.py

tiers.engine: FirmwareWorld (registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_fw.py) over the transpiled firmware in ds.Sim (registry/tests/_dump_sim.py): one real firmware, a strict entity registry, a UTC-true clock, an interval scheduler, NVS / Modbus fault policies and a full-boot reboot primitive
tiers.real_source: firmware/ecco_clock_dongle_stage3_4_free_power.yaml: the real Free Power and Dump to Grid START / END / restore / recovery / containment scripts, both 15 s watchdogs, the FULL on_boot except the FB durable boot read and two static_assert blocks, the manual TOU and register 244 Load / Apply buttons, the real poll scripts and their failure handlers
model_assumptions: synthetic SITE bank and telemetry (no site values); no inverter physics: export, SOC and PV change only when a scenario publishes telemetry
scripts and Modbus are synchronous: a START or a restore takes 0 ms, so a power cut lands between two firmware events, never inside a Modbus frame or an NVS write

the clock derives Europe/London local time from the UTC epoch with the hand-coded rule; only the first NTP sync per boot is modelled; interval timers are anchored at power-on (ESPHome's random interval offsets are not modelled, harness_limitations HL-10; same-tick watchdog order is an explicit parameter); script.execute runs the callee to completion inside the caller (HL-11); a scenario or finding whose verdict depends on this scheduler phase carries phase_sensitive true with the reason, and every corpus trace digest depends on it by construction

NVS commit policies wrap commit_record per instance: landed, not_landed, false_negative (stored, False), false_positive (nothing stored, True); boot faults: a single key read as ABSENT, read errors, a wrong-size blob, a whole-partition erase that also clears every preference

NVS fault cells (V0.1): false_negative models one ESP-IDF fault cell (the new copy stored and read at the next boot, the store healthy); the other cells after ESP_ERR_NVS_REMOVE_FAILED (an old copy resurfacing, a page refusing further writes) are not modelled, and the ESP-IDF semantics are REPORTED, not verified offline; a per-key read_error heals at the next plain boot, which is optimistic for a data CRC cause; read_error_all keeps the data, which in ESPHome exists only after a failed partition erase

NVS USED-KEY RULE (V0.1): a not_landed, false_negative or false_positive commit fault and a per-key read_error or wrong_size boot fault are refused with a harness error on a key never stored earlier in the run (no record under it now and no landed commit of it since the last whole-partition erase): the device route of a false negative needs an earlier stored version of the key; scenarios that inject on a marker key first complete a lease of that domain (a verified restore leaves the marker CLEAR). Coverage cost: the never-used forms are no longer exercised (an honest marker commit failure on a fresh device, the never-used ABSENT forms of the Phase-B marker false positive, the fresh-device register 244 lockout)
ESPHome preferences: only flushed values survive a power cut (1 s global poll plus the flash write interval)
a Modbus link model (reads no_response, writes timeout_lost) that also stops the telemetry / configuration polls; MODEL handlers replace the poll on_response lambdas that do not transpile
RTC correction lock windows are injected as correction_in_progress windows; the RTC tick itself is not executed in this tier
not executed: the 60 s clock read, the 1 s RTC tick, the FB housekeeping interval and the supervision shadow interval (they do not transpile)

tiers.engine: CoupledWorld (registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_ha.py): the HA script interpreter (home-assistant/tests/_ha_script_sim.py) running the real packages, with a RealDongle adapter that maps every dongle entity the packages use onto one FirmwareWorld (the hand-written dongle models are not used)
tiers.real_source: home-assistant/packages/ecco_free_power_schedule.yaml, home-assistant/packages/ecco_dump_to_grid_schedule.yaml, home-assistant/packages/ecco_schedule_manual_restore.yaml and the firmware of the firmware tier, under Europe/London time on a UTC-true timeline
model_assumptions: a firmware run executes synchronously at its gate instant; its Modbus ops, commits and publishes are projected onto the HA clock (op_s per op, except no_response_s 2.0 s for an op with a no_response outcome (the ESPHome Modbus hub's default send_wait_time) and timeout_s 3.0 s for an op with a timeout outcome (the firmware's bounded wait_until), commit_s per commit, the length of an explicit delay executed under a transaction lock, publish_s to HA); any other dongle mutation inside a projected transaction is refused loudly (UNSUPPORTED); a second press of a single-mode script whose own work is still pending is dropped and counted, a press of a script that is in the transaction only through a nested script.execute is refused loudly (UNSUPPORTED); package options the interpreter ignores are refused at load

latency defaults (press, command, op, publish, commit) are fixed parameters: the press-to-gate delay and the per-op time are derived from recorded transaction timings, the others are model values; one op time serves both domains
bus model: recorded busy windows, the lab's own poll traffic, or explicit synthetic windows; the watchdog phase relative to the HA clock is a sweepable parameter
ASSUMPTION: Home Assistant saves restore-state every 15 minutes and at a clean stop; a crash rolls every package helper back to its value at the last save; persistent notifications are not restored
ASSUMPTION: dongle entities read unavailable for a reconnect gap after an HA start or a dongle boot; polled counters read unknown until the new boot's first sample

ASSUMPTION: a service call to a dongle entity while the ESPHome API link is down is dropped silently (offline_policy 'silent', the default and the policy of most scenarios) or raises S.ServiceError before delivery (offline_policy 'raise', used by HF-09 and its corpus HF-09-a / HF-09-b); which one matches Home Assistant is not known offline

service-call faults: S.ServiceError (raised before delivery) is the interpreter's only modelled exception; HF-09 injects it per service name with the interpreter's fail_services hook inside its suite (not a replay action)
dump_plant is an opt-in plant stand-in for Dump leases (battery follows the written ceiling)
exact non-:00 time triggers through the interpreter's schedule_time_triggers helper

tiers.engine: RtcWorld (registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_rtc.py) over registry/tests/_fbd1_harness.make_rig (D1Sim) with the real Free Power START and its 15 s watchdog on the same simulator
tiers.real_source: the firmware's RTC read / correction lambdas and the Free Power START + watchdog of firmware/ecco_clock_dongle_stage3_4_free_power.yaml; ecco_rtc:: runs as the Python mirror registry/rtc_policy.py (header parity with firmware/include/ecco_rtc_policy.h is enforced only by registry/tests/test_rtc_policy.py, which needs a C++ compiler: ECCO_CXX when set, else the first of g++, c++, clang++ found on PATH; without one that check fails rather than skips)
model_assumptions: exact NTP wall clock (no jitter) with the hand-coded Europe/London rule; the inverter clock is the harness InverterRtc model (offset + rate)
the rig does not run on_boot; only the RTC read, the RTC tick and the Free Power watchdog intervals run
Free Power START inputs (battery voltage, configuration_online) are set as entity states because no poll runs
a D1Sim reboot is not modelled (refused loudly); a Dump lease cannot run on D1Sim, so RT-03 replays the extracted lock windows into a FirmwareWorld (split model)

invariants.meaning: inverter writes stay inside the write surface {22-24, 230, 232, 244, 250-261, 268-279}
Free Power and Dump to Grid are never both active
no domain writes 256-261 while the other domain holds a durable RESTORE_REQUIRED marker (tagged N17 when the other domain is corrupt)
no lease is active after a reboot without a new START
while a domain is corrupt-locked nothing writes its registers except the SG-02 literal 244 = 2

at steady points, owned registers that differ from the synthetic ORIGINAL have a RAM-visible obligation (snapshot valid or a corrupt / UNKNOWN lockout); tagged PLATFORM-ABSENT when an injected marker loss caused it
a due restore completes within a bound unless a lockout or an injected fault explains the delay
after the FULL on_boot a stored RESTORE_REQUIRED / PENDING_CLEAR / MALFORMED marker is mirrored in RAM
firmware truth never shows both leases active on the merged log
no write enable is left on while no schedule script runs (grace period)
SMR1 writes a staged number only while firmware truth shows no operation, lease or snapshot for that domain
the firmware override ends within the authorised window end plus a bound (the simulated overrun is recorded)
no new firmware session for a schedule run after the owner's End / cancel for that run
SMR1 never reports RESTORED while the owner's value is not on the number
an operator-facing lockout text names its real cause (scenario-local)
a failed START is reported by its real cause and counted once (suite-local)
a failed restore is retried on the bounded comms backoff 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 / 300 s
after a restart the owed Stop SOC (bound to the obligation's end epoch) supervises the restore; a missing SOC counts as reached once 90 s of uptime have passed

a Modbus link loss, or telemetry that keeps arriving unchanged (grid CT, battery power, SOC), during an ACTIVE Dump lease ends the lease with the firmware's own reason within its bound (frozen telemetry: test_lab_fw_runtime.frozen_end_violations)
a leaked transaction lock is never released by time; the lock-age monitor escalates within its bound and the owed restore then completes
Last End Reason keeps the first reason the current or last lease ended
no restore write inside an RTC correction lock window
a schedule never presses START again after a START gate passed
a scheduled run never ends without a STARTED / CANCELLED result or an alert
no new lease is started for a run the firmware ended at a reboot (coupled-level form of the no-resume rule)
a schedule never presses START into an active lease of the same domain
a blocker that clears inside the schedule's own retry budget is retried, not failed at once
a scheduled window is never lost without a failure alert
an arm is refused only for a real conflict of its own window
the HA dongle models match the firmware's failed-START behaviour
a schedule alert states the failure's real cause and current advice
FPS1's recorded result does not contradict an outstanding durable obligation
a local start runs at that wall time or is refused with a DST-specific reason
an admitted Dump lease overlaps no charge slot in real local time
normal-day control: a Dump lease that overlaps a charge slot is refused
a lease ends at its gate second plus its duration on the UTC epoch
one verified large correction after the clock change, within the design bound
no lease-end action inside an RTC correction lock window
no restore write inside an RTC correction lock window
a START inside an RTC correction lock window is refused with zero writes
while a restore obligation is owed only large corrections run (firmware equals the policy mirror)
the inverter clock error stays within 600 s
a stopped inverter clock is reported by the documented stall signal
London local time agrees with the two hand-coded oracles (and zoneinfo when importable)
every local wall time round-trips through UTC with its fold
fold / gap semantics follow zoneinfo (fold=0: first occurrence; gap: pre-transition offset)
every event log is UTC-monotonic, also across reboots and power cuts
millis() is the low 32 bits of the uptime; a lease across the wrap ends on its UTC epoch

scenarios.result_summary: PASS: a: the inverter acknowledges but never applies 244 := 2; both attempts fail on the 244 readback, 256-261 are contained at min(original, 500 W) and named so, the marker stays RESTORE_REQUIRED, one automatic retry, then the durable operator lockout; Force Restore Original completes once 244 is applied again. b: the 6-slot 256-261 write is acknowledged but not applied; both attempts fail on the readback, then the operator lockout, with 256-261 at 1000 W reported as a repeated mismatch. b2: a FOREIGN 261 makes the plan per slot and is never written; after a comms error on 260 every retry is a single-slot 260 write, acknowledged but not applied and failed on its readback, with no 'restored and verified' claim. b3-256 .. b3-261 (one per slot k): a FOREIGN slot (261, or 256 for b3-261) makes the plan per slot and is never written; every single-register write of k after the End (policy write:<k>x1) is acknowledged but not applied, so the first attempt (244 and every other slot written one by one) and the single-slot retry of k both fail on k's readback, then the operator lockout, with k at 1000 W reported as a repeated mismatch and no 'restored and verified' claim. b4-ct / b4-cb / b4-co (the containment path): every 244 write is acknowledged but not applied, so 244 is not proven and every non-FOREIGN slot is written at min(original, 500 W); the floor write of 258 (a FOREIGN 261 makes the plan per slot), the 6-slot floor block (nothing FOREIGN) or the floor write of 256 (put back to its ORIGINAL by the inverter, so not ECCO-owned, yet written by the containment) is acknowledged but not applied; both attempts fail on the readback, dump_restore_contained stays clear and every status says 'export may continue' (naming the FOREIGN 261 NOT CONTAINED), never 'ECCO's own at 500 W' or 'held at the 500 W floor', then the operator lockout. b5-lo: b3's shape for 259 on a site whose 259 ORIGINAL is 600 W, below the 1000 W lease value: the unapplied 259 reads above its expected value and both attempts fail on it. b6-ok: a fault-free restore of pairwise-distinct originals (3000/8000/7000/6000/4500/5000 W) verifies every slot against its own original in one attempt (RESTORED OK, marker CLEAR); b6-x257 / b6-x260: b3's shape for 257 / 260 on that bank with 256's / 259's original equal to the 1000 W lease value, so the unapplied slot reads its neighbour's expected value, and both attempts still fail on it. b7-rbnr / b7-rber (a failed readback in containment): b4-cb's / b4-ct's containment whose 256-261 readback gets no response / an error; the failure handler sets block_failed, so dump_restore_contained stays clear and every status says 'export may continue'; the 244 readback mismatch takes the mismatch path, so both attempts fail, then the operator lockout. b7-cmnr (the comms path in containment): 244 lands but its verify read errors, the 6-slot floor block is acknowledged but not applied and its readback gets no response: 'RESTORE WRITE FAILED' with 'export may continue' (backoff, marker kept); the retry after the backoff finds 244 ORIGINAL, restores ORIGINAL and completes. b7-ab (two attempts): the first containment attempt verifies and truthfully says 'held at the 500 W floor'; the inverter then puts 258 back to its ORIGINAL and the second floor block is acknowledged but not applied: the per-attempt reset keeps dump_restore_contained clear and no later status claims the containment. b7-af: every 256-261 slot FOREIGN, so the containment writes nothing, dump_restore_contain stays clear and every status names all six NOT CONTAINED with 'export may continue'. Every containment claim of every FW-09 timeline is backed by the bank at the instant its status was published (5 claims: a, c, b7-ab). c / c2: a failed 244 / 256-261 verify read fails the attempt on the comms path (backoff, marker kept; 244 unproven, so contained in c) and the retry after the backoff completes. Every core invariant holds. 23 negative controls killed (M9, C6 twice, MC244, MC256, the slot mutants C6k0..C6k5 and the loop-bound mutants C6s0 / C6s5, each killed by the b3 scenario of the slot it skips, C6k4 also by b2; C6bf (block_failed dropped) by the three b4 scenarios, C6om (the owned mask) by b4-co, C6lt ('<') by the three b4 scenarios and b5-lo, C6r1 (257 against 256's value) by b6-ok and b6-x257, C6r4 (260 against 259's) and C6v34 (259 / 260 swapped) by b6-ok and b6-x260; C6rh (block_failed dropped from every readback failure handler) by b7-rbnr, b7-rber and b7-cmnr, C6rn (the no-response handler only) by b7-rbnr and b7-cmnr, C6rs (the per-attempt reset of dump_restore_contained dropped) by b7-ab, C6m0 ('m != 0' dropped from the containment flag) by b7-af); c / c2 cannot kill M9 / C6 by construction (their failure path never runs the mutated readback compares), so they carry their own error-branch mutants. Model boundary: multi-register writes are all-or-nothing in the model (one outcome per operation), so a single unapplied slot is exercised on the per-slot plan only (a FOREIGN slot present, FW:20035, FW:20031) and the 6-slot block only whole (b4-cb all six unapplied, b6-ok all six applied); a partially applied 256x6 block is not modelled. The containment-claim helper judges each claim at its first publication (a status re-published unchanged is logged once) and takes ECCO's ceiling as the 1000 W START ceiling every FW-09 timeline shares.

scenarios.result_summary: Service exceptions against the real firmware (the interpreter's fail_services hook; S.ServiceError raised before delivery). A raised FPS1 START press is contained by continue_on_error: 'never reached the dongle' is true on the firmware's RAM gate-pass counter and the retry is one ordinary gated START (one lease). A DGS1 write-enable turn_on raising once presses nothing and starts on attempt 2; raising on every call reaches nothing and ends 'FAILED TO START - retries ended' with its alert. An SMR1 restore write raising 0.5 s after the firmware's own restore ends PARTIAL with the field named and one notification open (no false RESTORED). A raised closing turn_off is harmless because the firmware disarms the write enable at the press. A raised press plus a raised no-answer turn_off ends 'outcome unconfirmed, not retried' with an alert, the closing turn_off ending the switch off. F-HF09-1: when both turn-offs of a run fail after an unanswered press (three service errors, or one API outage of about 62 s or more from inside the press's flight under either offline policy) the write enable stays ON after the run, SMR1 stays OWED and the alert does not name the switch; a 40 s outage (HF-09-b) ends with the switch off. NC-HF09-1, NC-HF09-2 and NC-HF09-3 killed; NC-HF09-2b survives as expected on the scheduled path (the package's closing turn_off is the backstop) and is killed elsewhere on the owner-armed path (test_lab_selftest_firmware's owner-armed START check, HF-09.4 and the corpus trace digests).

scenarios.failure_outcome: an unclassified invariant violation (a new class: printed shrunk replay document, suite FAIL)
scenarios.result_summary: 160 quick sequences x 12 actions from published seeds (2000 in extended mode), all eight firmware invariants after every action and at quiescence: every violation matches a known signature and none is unclassified. The quick sequences hit partition erase 8 x (F-PB01-3 = F-FW04-4) and single-key false ABSENT 4 x (F-PB01-3:single-key = F-FW04-2); phantom admission (F-PB01-1 = F-FW01-1) and restore over a corrupt holder (F-PB01-2 = F-FW05-2) are pinned by corpus PB-01-a and PB-01-b, and the false-positive-commit signature (F-PB01-4 = F-FW06-3, its used-device form with the previous lease's stale CLEAR marker) by a directed section and corpus PB-01-d; the 2000 extended sequences hit restore over a corrupt holder once (a wrong-size blob on a stored marker), phantom admission 11 x, partition erase 42 x and false ABSENT 36 x, the false-positive-commit signature never. Every class duplicates a directed-suite finding, so none is counted here. NC-PB01-a, -b, -c and -d killed (ddmin shrinks the three random-search controls a, b and d to 2 actions each; c is a fixed directed trace); NC-PB01-a also exercises the unclassified-violation report path: its shrunk counterexample is printed as a replay document that survives the validate / dumps / load round trip and replays deterministically on the in-memory mutant, not on the real firmware. Generator constraints (harness_limitations HL-1 to HL-3 and HL-6): an operator Accept is issued only when it cannot move the lab's ORIGINAL (otherwise recorded as run_for 0), a register change is drawn as a foreign (inverter) write only while a domain holds that register, and an RTC lock window list is never empty; this narrows the searched operator actions and foreign writes. Since V0.1 a per-key boot fault (read error, wrong-size blob) and a commit-fault policy (not_landed, false_negative, false_positive) are drawn only on a key that holds a record (otherwise a plain reboot or run_for 0), and a whole-partition erase is not drawn while such a policy is armed, so no NVS fault hits a key never stored in the run (the lab refuses one); an event-log fault scan pins this in every run (quick: 8 commit faults and 8 per-key boot faults, none on a key without a record). The PB-01-a, PB-01-b and PB-01-d corpus documents start with one completed lease.

findings.severity: availability / cost precondition (low-medium): breaks the firmware's own R1 single-owner rule in the same runtime, but nothing is written in an unsafe direction until a third event
findings.confidence: high (mechanism, and the registry fit: PR41-GHOST is S4 decisions section 2.10 blind spot 1 plus the firmware's PR41 on_boot comment)
findings.reachability: trigger: nvs false_negative on a used Phase-B marker (fp.valid; dump.valid in the mirror order); device reachability: UNKNOWN pending the ESP-IDF host NVS test. INFERRED: a Phase-B marker false negative, whose only physical route is the marker's own nvs_set_blob error after the write (ESP_ERR_NVS_REMOVE_FAILED semantics, REPORTED; it needs an earlier stored version of the marker key, i.e. an earlier lease of that domain - modelled by the B5 completed-lease prelude; only one ESP-IDF fault cell is modelled); the firmware's 'unrelated pending key' route cannot reach the FP / Dump / reg244 marker commits, because ESPHome 2026.8.2 sync() clears its queue and the data commit's sync runs just before in the same lambda; rate UNKNOWN, likely very low; then any second START before a reboot (owner, or an HA FPS1 / DGS1 schedule that sees no snapshot)
findings.injected_primitive: nvs false_negative on a used Phase-B marker (fp.valid; dump.valid in the mirror order)
findings.needs_product_change_reason: firmware: keep the RAM mirror fail-closed at the Phase-B false-return branches (FP FW:9233-9240, Dump FW:18555-18558, reg244 FW:17204-17211) incl. the success branch's pacing reset FW:9184-9187
findings.model_dependence: MODEL: nvs_policy false_negative (the record lands, commit_record returns False) on the used Phase-B marker key after a completed lease of its domain (V0.1 used-key prelude); synchronous scripts; synthetic SITE and telemetry; a same-tick watchdog tie broken by an explicit wd_order (the extended phase sweep covers both orders)
findings.repair_scope: the two START scripts only: when the Phase-B marker commit returns false after the data record committed, keep the RAM mirror fail-closed (fill it exactly as the success branch does: snapshot_valid, marker_state RESTORE_REQUIRED, end epoch and intended targets, restore_requested) so the domain's own watchdog performs the existing verified no-op restore and commits CLEAR (a true negative is then also harmless); no new write path, every gate stricter; PR41 / S4 stay as the boot backstop; the reg244 Apply's analogous Phase B is a separate optional item (N10 / S4)

verification.classification_check: first matched to N15 as the closest registered id, with severity lowered to an availability / cost precondition; finally classified FINDING-KNOWN:PR41-GHOST (a registered known risk)

root_causes.title: A Phase-B marker commit false negative leaves a durable RESTORE_REQUIRED ghost with the RAM mirror clear: the other domain's START gate and HA's RAM-mirror sensors miss it until the next reboot
notes: [priority] P2 (V0: P1; P3 by likelihood). Mechanism CONFIRMED-IN-SIMULATION; device reachability UNKNOWN, likely very low (the trigger of RC-PR41-STRANDED-OVERRIDE; the harmful chain also depends on the ESP-IDF fault cell). The repair is cheap hardening.

[audit-reported, uncounted] Register 244 legs: (a) a reg244 ghost admits a genuine Dump lease and a reboot inside it gives the S4 dual lockout with 256-261 stuck; (b) a Dump ghost followed by the owner's reg244 Apply gives the S4 dual lockout on any later reboot (reg244 has no end time); (c) a lone reg244 phantom never self-heals and blocks Free Power, Dump and manual applies after any reboot; INV-NO-2ND-RESTORER cannot see the 244 pairs. Partly exercised: FW-03 boots a reg244 ghost together with a Dump ghost into the S4 dual lockout (F-FW03-1 / -2 / -3); the three legs as stated are not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

[audit-reported, uncounted] Repair scope: set the RAM mirror fail-closed at all three Phase-B false-return branches (Free Power FW:9233-9240, Dump FW:18555-18558, register 244 FW:17204-17211) and include the success branch's RAM pacing reset (FW:9184-9187), else a stale durable operator_needed holds the phantom; correct the stale comments (FW:1012-1020, 1088-1104); pin the data-to-marker commit adjacency (FW:9154-9159, 17182-17187, 18541-18547) that keeps the ESPHome 'unrelated pending key' route closed. A repair-scope statement: not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario (no scenario runs a repaired firmware).

[v0.1-observation, uncounted, untriaged] PB-01 extended generator seed 366 under the scratch ESPHome-like phase patch gives an UNCLASSIFIED INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE: a PR41-GHOST false negative on a used Free Power marker, a foreign inverter write of 126 to 268, then a second Free Power START (admitted, RAM clear) that snapshots 126 while the lab's ORIGINAL stays 20; either the foreign-register oracle limit (HL-2: a foreign change on a register held only by a ghost's durable marker is snapshotted by the ghost-admitted START) or a real ghost consequence (the true ORIGINAL 20 is overwritten in the data record); not seen on the lab's own phase; not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario or corpus document.

root_causes.title: Under the PR41 dual lockout a genuine Free Power override still applied has no in-firmware exit or time bound, and FPS1 / DGS1 keep showing ACTIVE with no lockout notification
root_causes.severity: cost / availability medium (stranded override); diagnostics medium (HA view); safety low
notes: [priority] P2 (V0: P1). Mechanism CONFIRMED-IN-SIMULATION; device reachability UNKNOWN, likely very low: a Dump marker own-key landed-then-error write (ESP-IDF REMOVE_FAILED on a key used before), ESP-IDF returning the new RESTORE_REQUIRED copy at the next boot (contested), a Free Power START in the same runtime and a reboot inside that lease. The consequence is severe, the trigger narrow and unverified.

[design-review] PR41 premise stale since fcp2: PR41 justifies the dual lockout with 'Dump's restore is unconditional/blind' (FW:1100-1104), but since the fcp2 ownership pre-read the Dump restore fresh-reads 244-261 and never writes ORIGINAL or FOREIGN slots (FW:19796-19808). With PR41's two '= true' lines removed in memory the bank returned to ORIGINAL in all 8 non-coincident combinations (audit); PR41 stays load-bearing only when the Free Power watts equal the ghost Dump ceiling or the two ORIGINALs diverge. The exit-less strand is a design-review item, neither 'by design' nor a defect yet; review it with SG-02 for Allow-Export sites.

[audit-reported, uncounted] Allow-Export sites (ORIGINAL 244 = 0): SG-02 writes 244 := 2 about 13 s after the boot and keeps it, so the owner's Allow Export becomes Zero Export indefinitely, and the containment text replaces the only status text that names the real cause. Partly reproduced: corpus FW-01-c (PASS, documented containment design) pins 244 = 2 and 'export CONTAINED' on such a site; the duration and the lost cause text are not asserted.

[audit-reported, uncounted] The Dump mirror strands a 256-261 battery-ceiling residue. Reproduced but uncounted: corpus FW-01-a pins 256 / 261 = 1500 W and HF-07-a pins 256-261 at the Dump ceiling (7000 W without the plant, model-dependent) under the lockout.

[audit-reported, uncounted] NVS-erase laundering: erasing NVS while locked clears the lockout but leaves the override silent, and the next Free Power START adopts it as ORIGINAL; a recovery procedure must restore the inverter first and only then repair NVS. Not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

[audit-reported, uncounted] 'Stated nowhere as accepted' is partly overstated: the PR41 test docstring intends 'once locked neither domain performs any further register write'. A source-reading statement: not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.
[coupling] Decide the HA alert for 'a function still active past its own lease end' together with RC-SAME-DOMAIN-SILENT-LOSS.

root_causes.title: A dual-lockout branch (PR41 or S4) retains no lockout cause, so the partner domain's status and every refusal text name the wrong cause
A ghost marker plus a later owner write: the next boot restores a stale ORIGINAL or locks out (no final-writer latch, N15)
root_causes.severity: owner intent / cost (low) with a diagnostics part

root_causes.title: P1 restores carry no cross-domain terms: with the other domain corrupt / UNKNOWN at boot a trusted restore writes the shared 256-261 over its unresolved obligation (N17)
The SG-02 containment gate has no other-domain obligation term and can overlay the Free Power lease's register-244 context (N16)
A held lease marker lost at boot (single key, read as ABSENT = CLEAR) leaves the override live with no visible obligation; a later START adopts the residue as ORIGINAL
root_causes.severity: Dump: safety (bounded); Free Power: cost; plus diagnostics
notes: [priority] P1 (unchanged). Mechanism CONFIRMED-IN-SIMULATION; device reachability PLAUSIBLE-UNDER-ASSUMPTIONS, rate UNKNOWN: the remaining route is ESP-IDF erasure of a corrupt entry (REPORTED by the S4 notes and the firmware's own 'do NOT reboot' text, FW:913; not verified offline); the second reboot needs no owner action (ESPHome's 15-min API / Wi-Fi reboot, safe mode, a power cut). Ruled out: a power cut between the ordered commits, key derivation, a tag rename and a 24-bit item-hash collision (test_fallback_nvs_keyhash.py).

[audit-reported, uncounted] In the READ_ERROR (UNKNOWN) state the safety census labels the domain 'a Dump to Grid restore is owed' (FW:20661-20662) and the gated Restart offers the override 'the boot path re-opens it' (FW:20693-20701), against the firmware's own 'do NOT reboot' (FW:913) and HA's 'Do NOT restart the dongle'. Not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.
[audit-reported, uncounted] The register 244 domain has the same ABSENT-to-CLEAR mapping (FW:982-985); no V0.1 scenario covers it. Not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

[audit-reported, uncounted] Repair design: the boot cross-check 'ABSENT marker and data active_persisted == 1 -> UNKNOWN lockout' also locks an idle domain whose CLEAR marker is lost after a clean end (the end commit keeps active_persisted = 1; Force and Accept refuse, no exit); the refined Dump check 'active_persisted == 1 and restore_requested == 0' removes those idle lockouts without a new commit; Free Power needs a data-record closure commit; a page-level loss defeats any data-record witness. Evaluated by the audit as in-memory mutants; not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

[audit-reported, uncounted] After the false ABSENT, HA can show a schedule-started lease as COMPLETED, and a saved fallback profile gives only a generic drift WARNING (HA is not completely silent then). Not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

root_causes.title: A whole-partition NVS erase at boot loses every marker and record: the override stays live and a Free Power START captures the Dump residue as ORIGINAL
root_causes.severity: safety (secondary, bounded); Free Power lease: cost

root_causes.title: A Phase-B marker commit that reports success without storing: the lease runs on RAM only and a reboot leaves the override live with a stale CLEAR marker (ABSENT on a never-used domain, a form the lab no longer injects since V0.1)
root_causes.severity: Dump: safety (bounded); Free Power: cost; trigger reachability UNKNOWN pending the ESP-IDF host NVS test (not labelled a model artefact)
notes: [priority] P3 (V0: P2) pending the ESP-IDF host NVS test; trigger UNKNOWN, not labelled a model artefact. No route exists at the ESPHome layer (ESPHome 2026.8.2 sync() returns success only when no pending set_blob failed); a physical ESP-IDF route via an INVALID page after one reported flash-op failure was described in the audit (medium confidence, not executed).

[v0.1-observation, uncounted, untriaged] With a used register 244 domain (a completed Apply / Restore first), an owner change 244 := 1 and then an Apply whose data-record commit is a lab false_positive (nothing stored, true returned) resolve at the next boot from the previous transaction's stale data record: the later Restore writes 2 ('RESTORED OK - register 244 confirmed back at 2'), not the true pre-Apply value 1, and no invariant fires: the lab treats the owner-initiated register 244 Restore's landed write as the owner's new ORIGINAL (_lab_fw OWNER_DOMAINS includes r244), so the stale value 2 becomes the baseline and the pre-Apply value 1 is not compared (by the same rule a stale-ORIGINAL restore through the r244 domain is invisible to INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE). An N15-like stale-ORIGINAL restore through a data-record false positive (compare RC-N15-STALE-ORIGINAL); trigger reachability UNKNOWN as F-FW06-2 / -3; Free Power and Dump are not affected (their START re-commits the data record after activation). Found by a V0.1 scratch probe; no directed scenario or corpus document pins it.

root_causes.title: A Free Power START commit failure runs the activation-failure branch too: the real cause is overwritten, failures count twice, and FPS1 copies the misleading final text
The Free Power restore has no link-recovery retry (the Dump SG-39 analogue)
notes: [priority] P3 (V0: P2): a bounded, cost-only parity gap. The Free Power restore comes 3-288 s after the link returns against 1-13 s for Dump (FW:10131-10136 has no link-recovery clause; the Dump SG-39 clause is FW:19776-19783).

root_causes.title: The Dump boot path attributes an already-ended lease's end to the restart
Export stays enabled when the inverter refuses every 244 write (documented SG-04 residual)
root_causes.severity: safety class, documented accepted residual, low in practice

root_causes.title: One failed configuration block read ends an ACTIVE Dump lease as TELEMETRY LOST (explicit fail-closed term with no stated rationale)
A lock leak recurring before every boot's first watchdog tick gives an unbounded stuck-lock restart loop (documented FCP2-F6 residual, refined)

The firmware end tail (end epoch fixed at commit, 15 s watchdog quantum, busy-bus deferral, multi-op restore) is not budgeted by the packages' window-end texts (FPS1 / DGS1: nothing starts or runs after the window end); the +30 s bound exists only as the HA suites' model-only check
notes: [documentation-test-bound] P3. '+30 s' is the HA test suites' model-only bound (home-assistant/tests/test_ecco_free_power_schedule_reliability.py:199, test_ecco_dump_to_grid_schedule_reliability.py:277, run against hand models whose session ends at start + duration), not a package claim; the package texts are 'nothing starts or runs after it' (FPS1:77, DGS1:90) and 'a late start ends within about a minute of the window end' (FPS1:26, DGS1:29). The 36 / 52 s overruns are phase-dependent examples on one recorded-busy-window bus model (idle-bus maxima about 15.9 s Dump / 19.4 s Free Power). Mechanism CONFIRMED-IN-SIMULATION as an existence claim.

root_causes.title: FPS1 / DGS1 startup recovery decides only from package helpers a crash rolls back and starts a new session after an End, a firmware end or a site power cut
root_causes.severity: low: owner intent / cost plus diagnostics
notes: [design-decision] P2 as a design-decision item (P3 on harm alone): whether a startup recovery may re-create a lease after an unclean Home Assistant stop or a site power cut is a policy question. Reachability rests on HA's restore-state cadence (a 15-min save), UNVERIFIABLE offline; the finding reproduces at about (900 - D) / 900 of rollback instants; FPS1 variant: the run's own success dismisses the recovery notice, so End & Restore is overridden silently.

root_causes.title: A crash during STARTING loses the SMR1 obligation and the recovery re-stage yields a false RESTORED (documented limit, understated consequence)
A graceful HA restart while STARTING, after the start helper was moved, abandons the run silently
The no-answer proof uses RAM-only attempt counters that a dongle reset clears
A cross-domain lease tail is treated as a persistent refusal: the next schedule fails at once although the blocker clears inside its retry budget
A same-function schedule at or inside the previous lease's end records BLOCKED with no failure alert and loses the window
notes: [coupling] P2 (low end). It comes from the documented rule 'already active = started' (FPS1:99 'BLOCKED - Free Power already active' and the alert condition that exempts it, FPS1:449 / :832; DGS1:135, :468, :905), not an alert oversight. Decide together with RC-PR41-STRANDED-OVERRIDE (F1): alert when a function is still active past its own lease end.

root_causes.title: DGS1's arm-time TOU walk reads the Free Power override's own grid-charge slots and refuses every Dump arm during a Free Power lease
An owner change within the restore write's latency is overwritten and reported RESTORED (documented limit, wrong documented consequence)
The HA dongle models keep a failed START's snapshot pending until End & Restore, unlike the firmware's automatic restore
DGS1's failed-start alert keeps 'press End & Restore Now' after the firmware restored
FPS1 records 'FAILED TO START - RESTORED OK' for an activation write / verify failure: the reason is lost
FPS1 / DGS1 arm validation has no DST guard: an ambiguous or nonexistent local start is resolved silently (fold=0) or refused with a misleading text
notes: [audit-reported, uncounted] Editing an already-armed start into the repeated hour is not re-validated and can start Free Power at once (reproduced by the audit in the coupled simulation; not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario); the repair scope extends to edits while armed. Mechanism PLAUSIBLE-UNDER-ASSUMPTIONS (HA fold=0 resolution not verifiable offline).

root_causes.title: The Dump START TOU gate (and its DGS1 mirror) walks local minutes: on DST change nights it admits a lease across a charge slot (SG-25, deferred)
root_causes.severity: safety (known, DEFERRED), qualified: practical impact low
notes: [audit-reported, uncounted] The SG-25 operational restriction (no Dump 00:00-03:00 local on a change night) is procedural only: no package or firmware guard exists (a cheap DGS1 arm-time refusal is possible later). F-HF08-3 and the RT-03 compound case reproduce the gate admitting the lease; the missing guard is a source fact, not reproduced by a V0.1 directed scenario.

root_causes.title: The battery range of the fast frozen-CT criterion is not re-seeded at START or outside a lease, so a CT already repeating at START meets the fast criterion on battery values from outside the repeat window
root_causes.severity: low: fail closed (an earlier lease end) and diagnostics (a misleading end text)

root_causes.severity: low: a write enable left on permits a START without the arm step; SMR1 restore blocked; diagnostics

harness_limitations.component: _lab_fw.accept_adoption (called by FirmwareWorld._adopt_if_clear): the lab's ORIGINAL after an operator Accept
harness_limitations.anchor: registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_fw.py: def accept_adoption(dom: str, pre: dict, post: dict, texts) -> dict:
harness_limitations.limitation: V0 adopted the live register bank as the new ORIGINAL after ANY operator Accept call (dump_accept, fp_operator ACCEPT_CURRENT_STATE) whose domain marker read CLEAR or ABSENT with no valid snapshot: also after an Accept the firmware refused, and also for the shared 256-261 while the other domain's lease held them. The V0.1 rule adopts it only after an Accept whose last published status is a firmware SUCCESS text (Free Power firmware :13644 / :13649, Dump :20936 and the residue form :20942-20943) that cleared an obligation the domain held before the Accept (stored marker CLEAR or ABSENT and the snapshot no longer valid), and never for a register another domain holds (snapshot, lockout, transaction, stored marker other than CLEAR / ABSENT, active lease). Residual: a Free Power Accept whose durable clear is pending (:13649, PENDING_CLEAR) adopts nothing and the later clear-only completion is not an Accept, so the oracle can keep the pre-Accept ORIGINAL
harness_limitations.effect_on_verdicts: V0: a check that compares the bank with ORIGINAL (INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE above all) could be wrong after such an Accept in both directions (a residue adopted as the baseline hid an override; the other domain's later restore to its own snapshot then differed from the adopted values, a false violation, PB-01 extended seed 929). The root fix changed no counted finding, no suite verdict and no corpus trace digest; one uncounted fw_durability FW-06 extended-mode run moved from resolved to visible (a refused Accept no longer adopts the Dump override). The residual can only give a false (loud) INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE, never a masked one: measured 1 such Accept in quick mode and 2 in extended mode (fw_durability FW-06 injection flows on foreign registers), with no violation
worked_around_in: test_lab_selftest_firmware: section [16d] pins the rule (the SUCCESS texts, a table of hand-built Accepts over every guard, positive controls, refused and no-op Accepts adopting nothing, the PB-01 seed 929 continuation with a Force Restore and no false INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE, each with the V0 rule run in memory as its control)

test_lab_property: PB-01 still issues an Accept only when it cannot move the ORIGINAL (any other drawn Accept is recorded as run_for 0); with the root fix this gate is redundant (without it the V0.1 rule gave 0 unclassified violations over 160 quick / 2000 extended sequences, the V0 rule 3 / 77, measured before the V0.1 NVS used-key rule changed PB-01's fault draws and not re-measured since) and is kept so PB-01's action statistics stay comparable
test_lab_fw_obligations: FW-01 to FW-03 judge each Accept by its own result text, the bank values and the durable marker, not by the ORIGINAL-based checkers
test_lab_fw_durability: the FW-06 Accept flows run with the domain's registers held and assert the commit outcomes directly
harness_limitations.status: fixed in V0.1 at the root (_lab_fw.accept_adoption); the PENDING_CLEAR residual stays open (a deferred adoption at the clear-only completion would need its own design)

harness_limitations.component: _lab_fw FirmwareWorld scheduler (_sched_reset, run_for), the coupled tier's polled template sensors (_lab_ha RealDongle) and the RTC rig's interval start: the interval phase MODEL
harness_limitations.anchor: registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_fw.py: first = j["startup_ms"] if j["startup_ms"] is not None else j["period_ms"]
harness_limitations.limitation: every executed firmware interval runs first at its declared startup_delay, else one full period, after power-on (uptime 0) with zero offset (plus the lab's own phase_ms sweep parameter) and is rescheduled at due + T (now + T only for a slot a raw advance already missed); the two ESPHome preference jobs are anchored at power-on likewise, the coupled tier samples its polled template sensors first one period after power-on and then on the uptime grid, and the RTC rig starts its intervals at a fixed phase. ESPHome 2026.8.2 runs an interval first at setup plus a random offset uniform in [0, min(T/2, 5 s)) (core/scheduler.cpp:21 MAX_INTERVAL_DELAY 5000, :107-111 calculate_interval_offset_, :182-184 first execution at now + offset; core/component.cpp:383 start_poller at setup; components/interval/interval.h:14-16, a startup_delay is a set_timeout followed by start_poller) and reschedules at now + T (scheduler.cpp:540). On the lab grid intervals with commensurate periods meet on the same millisecond: the 15 s Free Power and Dump watchdogs tie (their order is the explicit wd_order parameter) and the 10 s telemetry poll meets them every 30 s; every timing-bound check therefore sits on one phase
harness_limitations.effect_on_verdicts: a verdict that pins an instant, a same-tick order or a bound on the 5 s / 10 s / 15 s grid holds at the lab's phase only. Every check that failed under an in-memory ESPHome-like phase patch (first run at setup + startup delay + a seeded offset, reschedule at now + T; 17 quick configurations: 8 seeds of the full patch and 3 seeds each of three narrower or differently anchored variants; 3 extended seeds), every timing-bound check the independent audit named, and every check the V0.1 review found phase-dependent without a FAIL line (the HF-03 whole-site cut grid, whose F-HF03-2 pins can vanish while the point takes a held branch, and the test_lab_ha_lifecycle finding register) is tagged: 200 PHASE_SENSITIVE_TAGS prefixes in 13 suites (4 of them extended-only), 442 executed tagged checks in quick mode and 503 in extended mode (LAB-SUMMARY phase_sensitive), and 21 of 39 scenarios and 18 of 51 findings (11 of them counted) carry phase_sensitive true. Under the patch the exact pins of four counted reproductions fail: F-HF01-1 and F-HF04-2 in 17 of 17 configurations, F-HF04-1 in 14 of 17 and F-HF08-3 in 6 of 17. F-FW03-2's pin is composite (both explicit wd_order outcomes in one run: the Dump-first context hold with its operator exits and the Free Power-first N17 contrast) and fails in 17 of 17 by construction, while its Dump-first context-hold signature reproduces whenever the Dump watchdog's random offset is the smaller (the context hold with its operator exits in 10 of the 17). F-HF03-1 reproduces at both phases (4 of 6 swept points on the lab grid, 5 of 6 under the patch); F-HF03-2 reproduced at the 60 s and 120 s / 5 s whole-site cut points wherever its section ran, while the 5 s / 5 s point took the no-new-lease branch in 4 of the 5 configurations in which the section ran (its pin then absent with no FAIL line). The RC-FALSE-ABSENT, RC-PR41-STRANDED-OVERRIDE and RC-PR41-GHOST reproductions held under the patch; only their corpus trace digests, which replay one recorded timeline on the lab grid by construction, failed. The corpus FINDING documents FW-05-e, FW-06-a, FW-07-i3 and HF-05-b also fail an expectation under the patch (6, 11, 10 and 11 times in the V0.1 review's 11 patched quick configurations; on HF-05-b's fixed timeline the recorded deviation does not occur), while the suite pins of F-FW05-2, F-FW06-1, F-FW07-5 and F-HF05-2 hold; these four findings carry phase_sensitive true for that reason. In quick mode under the patch test_lab_ha_schedules (HF-04 / HF-06) ends without a LAB-SUMMARY in all 11 patched quick configurations of the V0.1 review and test_lab_ha_lifecycle in 12 of the 17 patched quick configurations above: both refuse an interleaving inside a projected firmware transaction (LabUnsupported, fail loud); test_lab_ha_lifecycle refuses the HF-03 whole-site cut at its first grid point at full-patch seeds 1 to 5, at seeds 1 to 3 of both narrower variants and at power-on seed 1, and completes at full-patch seeds 6 to 8 and power-on seeds 2 and 3, where the site-cut 5 s / 5 s point changes branch (F-HF03-2); extended mode adds LabUnsupported refusals in the ha_lifecycle and ha_phantom extended sections. At f11d85f (V0.1 commit 3) two more suites stopped in quick mode: test_lab_property on the PB-03-b replay refusal (an action due before the world clock) and test_lab_selftest_firmware on a ValueError in its same-tick watchdog self-test. Since V0.1 commit 4 test_lab_property records a replay exception as a FAIL of that document (tagged) and continues, the selftest_firmware same-tick checks fail (tagged) instead of raising, and test_lab_selftest_rtc runs its replay-engine controls on a draft recorded without its timeline-bound lock_windows expectation when record() fails; with patch seeds 1 to 3 these three suites end with a LAB-SUMMARY and every FAIL tagged. Re-run at f11d85f with patch seeds 1 to 3: the same counted reproductions fail; two test_lab_replay_corpus negative controls (NC-RC-1, NC-RC-4) also failed untagged, because their control document FW-06-a has timeline-bound expectations since its V0.1 used-key prelude. V0.1 runs those engine controls on the expectations that hold on the tree under test; with patch seeds 1 to 3 they hold

harness_limitations.component: registry/tests/_dump_sim.py Sim.execute (shared simulator) and _lab_fw StrictSim / LabEntity.is_running: script.execute runs the callee to completion inside the caller
harness_limitations.anchor: registry/tests/_dump_sim.py: return  # mode: single - dropped, exactly like ESPHome
harness_limitations.limitation: ds.Sim runs every script synchronously (wait_until and delay are no-ops, _dump_sim.py 'elif kind in ("wait_until", "delay", "logger.log"):'), so script.execute returns only after the callee's whole run, and a script counts as running only while it is on the lab's synchronous call stack. The re-entry drop the anchor line calls 'exactly like ESPHome' therefore matches ESPHome only where both agree that the script is running, and script.is_running() answers from the call stack. ESPHome 2026.8.2's ScriptExecuteAction only starts the callee (components/script/script.h:239) and the caller continues as soon as the callee suspends at a delay, a wait_until or a Modbus request; a single-mode script drops an execute while an earlier run is still in flight (script.h:79-87). The divergent forms: (C1) firmware work the caller runs after the call happens in the lab after the callee's whole remainder, on the device before it; (R) a second execute of a script at the instant its first run reached a suspension point is run again by the lab and dropped by the device (a crafted double-end Dump watchdog tick re-runs restore_dump_to_grid_snapshot and replaces RESTORED OK with END IGNORED); (ISR) is_running() reads false for a script whose run would still wait in its own delays on the device; (busy) in the coupled projection a caller kept on the stack by a nested execute would count as busy (MISS-HA-1, refused since V0.1, HL-12)
harness_limitations.effect_on_verdicts: measured at f11d85f (V0.1 commit 3; commit 4 changes no executed scenario or corpus trace) by a scratch observation hook that changes no output (every suite identical with and without it, runtimes masked), quick / extended, scenario suites plus replay corpus: C1 1272 / 6515 (self-tests 23 / 23), in three patterns, all Dump: the watchdog's request_dump_end -> restore_dump_to_grid_snapshot then the watchdog's next branch 800 / 3622, the watchdog's dump_controller_tick then a lambda 461 / 2824, and dump_force_restore_original -> restore then the arm turn-off lambda 11 / 69; in each the caller's later work reads state the lab's restore already completed. The double-end form (R within one world step) occurs 0 / 0 times (the crafted probe gives 1); a same-instant re-execute from a separate world action at 0 ms spacing occurs 183 / 1715 times (self-tests 0 / 1: repeated START presses, telemetry polls at a slot instant, configuration polls), which the device would drop while the first run is in flight; is_running() is evaluated 0 / 0 times (its firmware uses sit in paths no scenario reaches or behind a condition that is false there); no execute is dropped and no non-single script is re-entered (0 / 0). No catalogued verdict is known to rest on these forms, but the lab does not detect them: in the firmware tier they pass silently
worked_around_in: test_lab_selftest_coupling: section [16] pins the coupled-tier half: a START press while START is in the projected window only through its nested restore execute raises LabUnsupported (MISS-HA-1), and a press while the pressed script's own work is pending is still dropped, as ESPHome's single mode drops it
harness_limitations.status: open: an asynchronous script model, or a lab-side detector that turns C1 / R occurrences into UNSUPPORTED points, is not implemented, and _dump_sim.py is a shared interpreter the lab does not modify; turning C1 into UNSUPPORTED would mark most Dump watchdog lease ends unsupported

harness_limitations.component: the lab's fail-loud rule: the _lab_ha projection, same-script press rule and package / runtime guards, the _lab_fw StrictSim allow-lists and NVS used-key rule, the replay engine and the suite output contract
harness_limitations.anchor: registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_ha.py:   - Interleaving inside a firmware transaction (fail loud instead, see Projection), Modbus latency beyond the per-outcome
harness_limitations.limitation: fail loud covers only the constructs the lab detects: then the scenario is a FAIL, BLOCKED or an UNSUPPORTED point, never a PASS. Since V0.1 that includes, in the coupled tier, an interleaving anywhere in a projected transaction whose window now lasts by op outcome (no_response 2.0 s, the ESPHome 2026.8.2 hub send-wait; timeout 3.0 s, the firmware's bounded wait_until; op_s otherwise; plus a delay executed under a lock), so the V0 projection gap is refused (ISS-HA-2); a same-script press while the script is busy only through a nested script.execute (MISS-HA-1; a press while its own work is pending is still dropped, as the device drops it); package options the interpreter ignores (a static guard at load), template values whose truthiness differs from Home Assistant's condition rule and input_number values outside the helper's range (runtime guards; ISS-HA-5); and in the firmware tier an injected NVS fault on a key never stored earlier in the run. Still silent: the duration of lock-free delays and polls (zero projected time), Modbus turnaround and queueing behind another firmware run, a wait_until whose condition is false in the lab (skipped where the device blocks up to its timeout), the synchronous script.execute forms (HL-11), the scheduler phase (HL-10) and the signedness of u-suffixed literals, which the transpiler drops
harness_limitations.effect_on_verdicts: a PASS means the run met no detected unmodelled construct, not that the device would behave the same where the lab is silent. Measured at f11d85f (V0.1 commit 3; commit 4 changes no executed scenario or corpus trace), quick / extended, scenario suites plus replay corpus: projection-gap interleavings 0 / 0, nested-only presses 0 / 0, transactions with a no_response or timeout op or an in-lock delay 0 / 0, ignored package options 0 / 0 (247 / 708 package-set checks), truthiness refusals 0 / 0 (283424 / 881859 values), input_number refusals 0 / 0 (2665 / 7503 writes); silent: lock-free delays met inside coupled runs 77664 / 286912 and explicit delays skipped by the firmware simulator 171176 / 826468, Modbus ops of two different world steps at one firmware instant 1961 / 8914 (of 342703 / 1628134 ops, each taking 0 ms in the firmware tier), skipped false wait_until 87 / 186 (every one after a timeout or custom_response outcome: a duration-only divergence), transpiler gaps 0 (no `continue` or `sizeof` site, 0 snprintf outputs longer than their buffer, 0 out-of-range values at the 5 unreduced unsigned sites). The V0.1 corrections turned no previously passing scenario UNSUPPORTED; the existing refused-interleaving points (test_lab_ha_lifecycle 2, test_lab_ha_schedules 8 in extended mode) lie outside the projection gap
worked_around_in: test_lab_selftest_coupling: sections [15] to [18] pin the per-outcome projection (the ISS-HA-2 probes refused with no_response and timeout, the same press applied after the corrected window, an in-lock delay extending the window), the MISS-HA-1 refusal and the own-work drop, the static guard (the real packages pass; enabled: false and 25 other injected constructs are refused) and the runtime truthiness and input_number guards
test_lab_selftest_firmware: section [8b] pins the NVS used-key refusal for every refused commit mode and boot fault, with the same faults on a used key accepted
test_lab_ha_lifecycle: sweep points that meet a refused interleaving or an unclassified harness outcome print an UNSUPPORTED line, never PASS (3 ids, 5 points in quick mode)
test_lab_ha_schedules: the extended HF-04 interleaving sweep prints its 8 refused points as UNSUPPORTED (HF-04-UNS-EXT)

harness_limitations.component: _lab_fw oracle checkers: INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE's explanation rule, INV-RESTORE-BOUND's excuse set and the invariant set (no SG-02 containment checker)
harness_limitations.anchor: registry/tests/assurance_lab/_lab_fw.py:         if not diff or vis:
harness_limitations.limitation: (1) INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE accepts any RAM-visible obligation (a valid snapshot mirror or a corrupt / UNKNOWN lockout of fp, dump or r244) as explaining every differing owned register (the anchor line; quiet_state's 'silent' uses the same rule); it does not map a register to the domain that owns it, although DOMAIN_REGS exists, so an override of a Free Power register while a Dump obligation is visible, or under any lasting lockout, stays masked while that obligation is visible. (2) INV-RESTORE-BOUND's excuse set is filled by any injected fault, power-off, cut, link-down, bus-busy, lockout or long-lock observation inside the due period and is reset only when a new period opens, so one short excuse explains the whole period however long the restore then takes (the mechanism HL-4 states). (3) No invariant checks SG-02 containment: INV-LOCKOUT-QUIET only whitelists the literal 244 = 2 write (check_lockout_quiet, 'SG-02 containment literal') and INV-NO-SILENT-OVERRIDE is satisfied by the lockout itself
harness_limitations.effect_on_verdicts: each can only miss a violation, never create one. (1) a white-box override of 230 during a Dump lease stays masked while dump.snap or dump.corrupt is visible (a V0.1 reproduction probe). (2) measured at f11d85f (V0.1 commit 3; commit 4 changes no executed scenario or corpus trace) with a scratch counting copy of the checker that returns the original result in every call (quick / extended, scenario suites): 580 / 3955 over-bound evaluations are excused (246 / 1339 distinct due periods; the audit counted 540 at the V0 HEAD), 474 / 2908 of them by a lockout; a true latch, the excuse no longer active for more than the 60 s bound before the completion or the end, occurs 4 / 68 times (3 / 38 distinct periods): Free Power restores that wait out their comms backoff after the link returns (the F-FW07-1 mechanism; test_lab_fw_runtime, 1 period in quick mode, 4 in extended mode), one Dump period each in test_lab_fw_runtime and test_lab_ha_schedules, and 32 distinct PB-01 extended-mode periods (mostly restores still open at the end of the sequence, the last Modbus fault 63 to 296 s earlier), not triaged; the replay corpus has none (37 / 74 excused). (3) a mutant whose Dump watchdog never arms containment (the audit's M5: a metadata-corrupt Dump lockout leaves 244 = 0, Allow Export) passes all eight invariants; at f11d85f it is killed only by directed checks and corpus replays (test_lab_fw_durability 'FW-04 guard', test_lab_fw_obligations 'FW-01 (a)' and its SG-02 variant, test_lab_ha_phantom 'a: no ECCO write during the lockout except SG-02 containment', the FW-01 / FW-04 / FW-05 / HF-07 replays)
worked_around_in: test_lab_fw_runtime: FW-07-A, FW-07-B and FW-07-F measure the restore delay after a link recovery directly and FW-07-A / FW-07-I rebase INV-RESTORE-BOUND at the recovery or the boot (the latch, as HL-4)
test_lab_fw_obligations: FW-01 asserts the SG-02 containment writes (only the literal 244 = 2, CONTAINED) and the per-register bank values directly, not through the checkers
test_lab_fw_durability: the FW-04 guard asserts that containment writes only 244 := 2 under the fail-closed lockout
test_lab_ha_phantom: the HF-07 chains assert that the only ECCO write during the lockout is SG-02's 244 := 2
harness_limitations.status: open: a per-register explanation rule, expiring excuses and an SG-02 containment invariant are not implemented; the audit predicts that the first two re-find only already-counted findings (F-FW07-1, F-FW08-1), which V0.1 did not test

intersections.gap: the existing coverage is graceful restarts against the dongle model; the lab's crash rollback rests on the 15-min restore-state ASSUMPTION (not measured) and real ESPHome reconnect timing is not modelled

the existing coverage is a Python model; the lab runs the real firmware, but the physical trigger (a same-key NVS error after the write) is REPORTED from the ESP-IDF documentation, not verifiable offline, and its rate is UNKNOWN; since V0.1 the lab injects it only on a key stored earlier in the run (one ESP-IDF fault cell, the other cells not modelled)
a cut inside a Modbus frame or an NVS write (a torn record) is not modelled; in the coupled tier a cut inside a projected transaction is UNSUPPORTED (HF-03-UNS-1)
owner edits inside a projected firmware transaction are UNSUPPORTED (HF-05-UNS-1, HF-05-UNS-2); the restore-write race window rests on model latencies
the lock leak is a white-box RAM injection (no leaking code path that overlaps a lease is known); Fallback Review / Save mutex holds are UNSUPPORTED (FW-08-U2)

the polls run with MODEL on_response handlers; frozen telemetry with the link up (FW-07-I) needs the meter-noise MODEL off for the whole world, so every poll slot is set explicitly and the SOC changes only when a scenario sets it (no SOC physics); NTP loss after a first sync is UNSUPPORTED (FW-07-U1)
a Dump lease cannot run on the RTC rig (split model with injected windows); windows beyond the 90 s breaker are UNSUPPORTED in the firmware tier (FW-08-E-U1)
SG-25 reproduces (known, deferred); the inverter executing its TOU on its own clock is not modelled (in-slot seconds INFERRED)
torn records and a cut between save() and sync() are not modelled; the lab boots through the FULL on_boot where the existing sweeps use boot slices
only the Phase-B marker false negative is driven through Home Assistant; the HA system-health mapping of the lockout is UNSUPPORTED (HF-07/system-health)
the early-reset case is a PROXY (grade INFERRED); later in-transaction cuts are UNSUPPORTED (HF-03-UNS-1)
the existing window-end check runs against the model's instant end; the lab sweeps the watchdog phase and bus traffic, which are not measured on hardware
the outcome depends on the HA versus dongle boot order (swept by down times); real reconnect timing not modelled
the HA target-SOC editor path under a phantom obligation is source-read only, not executed
the same-tick watchdog order is a lab tie; both orders are swept (on hardware each boot draws a random order)
the existing SMR1 premise (End & Restore required after a failed START) holds only for the HA models

a raised service call (S.ServiceError before delivery, the interpreter's only modelled exception) is injected per service name inside the HF-09 suite; no replay action injects it (harness_limitations HL-9), so only the api_outage form (HF-09-a, HF-09-b) is pinned in the corpus
